note: Errata 29, which overturns 26 on the inventory. Verbs stay three columns of four on the left; the inventory is now a GRID OF ICONS on the right where the text list was, scroll arrows at the right edge, sentence line full width above. Geometry lives here rather than in Screen.ts because two things read it: the engine, and the Python that renders the panel for review.

verbs.note: SCUMM had twelve verbs in three columns of four. We have nine, per Bible v2, so the fourth row carries the MENU button instead of three more verbs -- the grid is the reference's shape and no cell is left empty.

inventory.note: Eight visible, the top of ruling 29's six-to-eight. Four columns of 30px across the 122px column, two rows of 21. The ITEM NAME still draws in the sentence line on hover and on selection -- ruling 29 condition 1, and it is not optional: an icon must never be the only way an item is identified, which is also why ruling 26's authored display names stand unchanged.

arrows.note: Drawn as triangles, not typed. The 5x7 face has no arrow glyph and adding one would put an interface shape into the writing font.

mapButton.note: Doc 20 rule 2: the map is ALWAYS reachable. A hotspot in one room cannot satisfy that, so the map opens from the panel and not from a doorway. It sits in the verb grid's fourth row beside MENU, in geometry errata 26 already allocated and left empty -- nine verbs fill three rows of three, and the fourth row had one cell used and two spare.
